facts.fact: Cabo Verde's Casa do Cidadão publicly launched the Participa Cidadão app on 1 February 2017 as an online channel for complaints, suggestions and praise about public services; no case numbers are given.

The Ombudsman and Casa do Cidadao signed a service-level agreement on 19 January that makes the eparticipa.gov.cv platform available for citizens' complaints, reports and suggestions to the Ombudsman, plus a free green line; no case numbers are given.

note: Nothing stated on a digital channel for complaints about public services.
Complaints about banks and insurers reach the central bank by email, in person and in the complaints book; no government web portal, app or messaging channel on public services is stated.

facts.fact: Minister Edna Oliveira said the E-participa platform lets citizens submit complaints, reports and suggestions on the conduct of public services; no case figures given.
The labour inspectorate (IGT) launched its portal on 2026-11-03 letting workers and employers file labour complaints online; no number of complaints received is given.
facts.system: Portal e Sistema Integrado de Gestão da IGT

note: Only UNEP's project grievance mechanism is described, not a government channel for public-service feedback.
The Yes names eParticipa, already held.

facts.fact: The eParticipa page shows a public ranking of institutions by their share of citizens' participations answered: Casa do Cidadao 100%, INPS 8%, DNAP 3%; the page is undated, so the as_of is the inferred 2026 publication year.

note: Same speech by Minister Oliveira as CPV-003; no case count.

facts.fact: The ILO says a new General Labour Inspectorate portal, launched in Praia on 3 November 2026, lets users submit complaints about labour violations, attach documents and track case status online, with no complaint counts given.
facts.system: IGT portal and Labour Inspection Management Information System (SIGT)
